title: Derived homology-couple pages as representative quotients
statement: Let C be abelian [def-sp-abelian], and let F be the category of finite filtered cochain complexes [def-sp-filtration]. Suppose boundary inclusions hBZ and isomorphisms eH:Q_1^(p,q)(V) to H^(p+q)(gr^p V) are given for all V, with eH normalized by an epic representative projection z and a graded cycle lift g such that z pi eH=g pi_H [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Fix a finite filtered complex $U$ and the concrete homology couple $X$ of [def-sp-filtered-homology-exact-couple]. For each $r\ge1$ let $D_r$ be any representative differential [lem-sp-filtered-complex-page-differential] on $Q_r^{p,q}=\operatorname{coker}(B_r^{p,q}\to Z_r^{p,q})$. There exist isomorphisms $e_Q(s,p,q):(X.\operatorname{pageCouple}(s)).E^{2p+q,-p}\simeq Q_{s+1}^{p,q}$ for every natural $s$ and integer $p,q$. At $s=0$ their morphisms agree, as heterogeneous equality, with $(e_0^{p,q}\circ e_H^{-1})$. For every $s$, $e_Q$ intertwines the exact-couple differential with $D_{s+1}$, with target $(p+s+1,q-s)$ and the corresponding exact-couple index transport. This statement contains no supplied spectral sequence, no page-homology choices, and no first connecting comparison for the two-step quotient sequence.

proof.text: At stage zero take the equality isomorphism e_0 followed by eH inverse. The normalization hypothesis identifies the quotient projection with canonical graded homology.

Induct on s using the derived-couple restriction equations. Differentiating a representative computes its differential. Correct a representative by an incoming current boundary precisely when its differential can be put one filtration step deeper. Thus the outgoing kernel is the successor cycles modulo current boundaries; the incoming image is successor boundaries modulo current boundaries. Take the quotient of this kernel by that image to identify the next E term with Q_(s+2). The same differentiation formula and epic representative-cover cancellation identify the next differential with the specified D_(s+2).
